Subject: Custodian certification + escrow pathway -- initial ask

Hi Emily / AuditorOps team,

Thanks for the call this morning. HealthCore has asked that we provide a short cert matrix showing which parties have access to customer-controlled keys (BYOK/custodian keystores) when they choose our Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment, plus an outline of our subprocessor notification plan for any escrow or escrow-adjacent access scenarios.

Two quick asks to get moving:
- Can AuditorOps confirm the evidence format you need (spreadsheet + signed cover letter vs. audited SOC excerpt)?
- Emily, can you confirm whether HealthCore requires subprocessors to be notified before contract signature or only at operational handover?

I attached a draft matrix that maps roles -> access type -> conditional controls (see "custodian-cert-matrix.xlsx"). This is a first pass — Naomi and Irene, please flag anything we should not commit to in the matrix.

Proposed timeline: provide a refined matrix and a short cover note to AuditorOps by COB Monday (11/30). If that works, I will also kick off the internal subproc notification plan and loop in Legal for redlines to the DPA.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Custodian certification + escrow pathway -- initial ask

Thanks Ben — quick clarifications from an ops/legal perspective: 

1) Custodian roles: the matrix should separate (a) customer-managed CMKs stored in their KMS/HSM, (b) customer-kept keystores we install in-customer-network (air-gapped), and (c) Redwood-managed keystores used only when customer opts out of BYOK. For (a) and (b) operator access is extremely limited; for (c) we have standard access controls.

2) Escrow scenarios: We do not proactively escrow customer CMKs. Escrow only occurs under a documented legal hold or mutually agreed exception (e.g., court order, contractually negotiated escrow for specific regulated customers). If HealthCore wants an escrow pathway, Legal needs to approve language and a list of subprocessors who would be notified.

3) Data transfer and EU flow: If keys are customer-controlled and remain in their VPC/HSM, we can state no key material leaves the tenant. However, telemetry and audit logs will need to be scoped — we should give HealthCore a telemetry minimal set and a sample log extract.

Karthik/Irene: can you review the attached matrix and add the operational notes column (what evidence we can provide for each row)? I can then work with Legal to produce the redlined DPA points.

Naomi
--
Naomi Feldman
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

Hi team,

Thanks for the draft. A few points from the auditor side: 

- Evidence format: a populated spreadsheet (like your draft) + a short attestation letter from Redwood Security is sufficient for initial review. If HealthCore requires an independent attestation, we'll note that as next step.
- Subprocessors: please provide a list of subprocessors with the role, region, and whether they will have any possibility of accessing key material. A YES/NO on key access per subprocessor is fine.
- Data transfer: for EU-resident data, if key material never leaves EU control (customer-managed in-region HSM or customer keystore inside EU VPC), mark "no transfer" in the matrix. For cases where we route logs or telemetry to Redwood systems, identify the specific fields and whether they are pseudonymized.

Could you also include a redlined DPA excerpt that captures: (1) explicit statement that customer CMKs never leave customer-controlled HSMs except under specified legal/contractual exceptions, and (2) the notification process for subprocessors and escrow events (who signs, SLA to notify, and sample notification template)?

We can take an initial look at the spreadsheet if you send the refined version by 11/30. Also please attach any sample logs or telemetry extracts you intend to share.

Regards,

Emily / Daniel / team — thanks for the quick feedback. Action plan below and owners/times: 

1) Matrix update (Ben/Naomi): refine rows to explicitly cover BYOK-in-customer-HSM, customer-keystore-on-prem, and Redwood-managed KEKs; add "evidence we can provide" column and mark transfers. Deliverable: updated spreadsheet and one-page attestation for AuditorOps. Due: Mon 11/30 EOD.

2) Telemetry sample (Irene): produce a pseudonymized sample log extract and upload to the shared drive. Deliverable: "telemetry-sample.csv"; link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeid/CertMatrix. Due: Mon 11/30 5pm PT.

3) DPA redlines (Irene/Legal): Irene will prepare a DPA excerpt capturing the "no key material leaves customer HSM absent legal/contractual exception" clause. Legal to propose notification SLA for subprocessors and escrow events (recommended: 10 business days pre-notice for planned subprocessors; 48 hours for emergency legal/compelled access). Deliverable: dpa-redlines-v3.pdf. Due: Tue 12/01 COB.

4) Subprocessor list (Karthik): compile the list of infra and third-party vendors that touch telemetry or backups and indicate YES/NO for key-material access. Deliverable: subproc-list.csv. Due: Tue 12/01 COB.

Next steps for HealthCore: Emily, once we submit the updated package on Monday, can you confirm whether HealthCore requires subprocessors to be notified pre-signature or at operational handover? If pre-signature, we'll tie the notification timeline into your contracting window.

I attached the updated draft matrix and a short sign-off template for subprocessor notification (custodian-cert-matrix.xlsx; subproc-notify-template.docx). Naomi/Irene please review before we send.

Thanks everyone — will follow up Monday morning with the package.
